About Me

Who I Am

I am an Industrial Engineer with a research focus at the intersection of computer vision, edge AI, and industrial systems. My engineering background in mechatronics grounds my work in production constraints I study systems that must operate reliably under real physical conditions, not just controlled benchmarks.

My research thread runs through three interconnected problems: intelligent perception on resource-constrained hardware (TinyML on Jetson/embedded devices for froth classification in mining), semantic segmentation for structural diagnostics (YOLOv7/v8 crack detection), and AI-driven document understanding for industrial supply chains. These share a common research question how can machine intelligence be made both accurate and deployable in high-stakes physical environments where latency, interpretability, and hardware limits are hard constraints?

I am actively seeking a PhD position to pursue this direction at depth contributing to the foundational understanding of edge ML systems and their application in industrial and safety-critical contexts.

project_01 · Monce · Dec 2025 – Feb 2026
Intelligent Document Processing Pipeline
for Automated EDI Generation
🌐 Remote AI Engineering · Pipeline Architecture · OCR Research
OCR Accuracy Improvement
Designed and implemented a 7-stage AI pipeline that transforms raw PDF/image documents (glass manufacturing orders) into structured EDI files. The system combines document intelligence, unified LLM extraction, hierarchical business rule application, semantic product matching, multi-layer validation, auto-correction, and deterministic output formatting replacing a fragile 3-agent architecture with a robust, auditable, self-healing pipeline.

Document Analyzer
ClassificationOCR Quality
"What am I looking at?"
Performs pre-extraction document intelligence: classifies document type, detects measurement units, assesses OCR quality, identifies client logos and table structures. This context-first approach prevents downstream unit confusion and allows dynamic strategy selection.

project_02 · Arcturus Technologies · Sep 2023 – Dec 2023
Applicare Insight: Real-Time Transaction
Monitoring with AI & ML
🌐 Remote (USA) ML Engineering · Clustering · Anomaly Detection
Fraud & Slowdown Detection
Designed and evaluated a suite of machine learning models to power Applicare's real-time transaction monitoring platform. The project combined unsupervised clustering to identify behavioral patterns, supervised classification to detect slow transactions, gradient boosting for feature importance analysis, and a neural network for high-accuracy prediction enabling the platform to distinguish normal vs. slow transactions and pinpoint the root-cause features driving latency.
modeling_pipeline 5 stages (eda + 4 models)
01
Data Collection & EDA
Preprocessing Feature Engineering
"What does the data look like?"
Ingested transactional user-experience data with 12 features covering timing, geography, and browser metadata. Performed correlation analysis, filled missing values via median imputation, and applied one-hot encoding for categorical variables. The correlation matrix revealed strong co-linearity between dom_ready_time, resource_fetch_time, and resp_available_time key signals for latency modeling.
Raw features (12)
str_total_time · str_backend_time
str_network_time · str_rendering_time
dom_download_time · dom_process_time
serv_conn_time · resource_fetch_time
browser · server · country · city
Preprocessing steps
✓ Drop ID/metadata cols
✓ Median imputation for nulls
✓ One-hot encoding (browser/server)
✓ MinMax + StandardScaler applied
02
K-Means Clustering
Unsupervised Elbow Method
"Can we separate fast from slow transactions?"
Applied K-Means (k=2) to normalized transaction data, using the elbow method to determine the optimal cluster count. Cluster 0 averaged ~800ms total time; Cluster 1 averaged ~1,200ms cleanly partitioning normal vs. slow behavioral groups without labeled data. These cluster labels became the supervision signal for downstream models.
Cluster 0 Normal
avg total_time ≈ 800ms
Fast DOM load · low backend lag
Majority of transactions
Cluster 1 Slow
avg total_time ≈ 1,200ms
High resp_time · backend bottleneck
Targeted for deep analysis

~800ms
Cluster 1 (slow)
~1,200ms
03
Decision Tree + K-Means
Supervised Explainability
"Why is a transaction slow?"
Trained a Decision Tree Classifier (max_depth=5) on the slow cluster to produce human-interpretable rules. The model identifies the decision boundaries that predict whether a transaction within the slow segment is flagged slow (top 25th percentile). Provides full textual and visual explainability a key requirement for Applicare's engineering team to act on insights.
Training target
is_slow = total_time > Q75
Binary: Fast (0) / Slow (1)
Trained on slow cluster only
Output
✓ Visual tree (depth 5)
✓ Textual rule export
✓ Feature split thresholds
04
Gradient Boosting Regressor
Feature Importance Root Cause
"Which features drive slowness?"
Applied a Gradient Boosting Regressor to the slow cluster to rank features by their contribution to total transaction time. Results showed resp_time (~40%), rendering_time (~21%), and resource_fetch_time (~19%) as the dominant latency drivers actionable targets for Applicare's platform optimization team.

05
ANN and MLP Classifier
Deep Learning Final Model
"Can a neural network predict slow transactions?"
Trained an MLPClassifier (hidden layers: 10 neurons, 1000 max iterations) on K-Means cluster labels as the target. The ANN converged steadily from loss 1.12 → 0.62 over 25+ epochs, achieving 62% overall accuracy. Weighted F1 of 0.61 confirmed consistent performance across classes providing a baseline neural approach for Applicare's real-time monitoring integration.

project_03 · FST Settat · Apr 2021 – Jul 2021
Design & Modeling of a Jet Engine:
An Alternative Approach Using Induction Heating
📍 Settat, Morocco Capstone Project · Mechanical Design · Thermodynamics
CATIA V5 · Induction Heating
Two-part capstone combining digital modeling and physical prototyping. Part 1: full dual-flow jet engine in CATIA V5 fan, compressors, combustion chamber, turbines, and nozzle in Assembly Design. Part 2: single-flow prototype built with an alternative combustion approach induction heating (W = R·I²·t) replacing conventional kerosene ignition.
project_structure 2 parts · digital + physical

Part 1 CATIA V5 Digital Model
CAD / 3D Modeling Assembly Design
"Model every component of a dual-flow jet engine"
Modeled all major components of a twin-stream jet engine using CATIA V5 Part Design, Generative Shape Design, and Assembly Design. Components were individually designed, then assembled on a common shaft. The casing was rendered in partial section to allow internal visibility during the assembly process.

C2
Part 2 Physical Prototype + Induction Heating
Prototyping Electromagnetics Thermodynamics
"Build a real engine using induction heating instead of kerosene combustion"
Constructed a single-flow jet engine prototype from physical components. The key innovation: replacing the conventional kerosene combustion chamber with an induction-heated temperature-rise chamber a coil wrapped around an insulator, powered by AC current, functioning analogously to a microwave chamber. Thermal energy is governed by W = R·I²·t, where R is the coil impedance jLω (dependent on inductance L and angular frequency ω).
Physical components built
Blower: 87mm radius · 12 blades
Motor-driven (blower + compressor)
3-stage axial compressor
Induction heating coil (AC-powered)
Convergent nozzle
Outer casing (hand-fabricated)

project_04 · Reminex Mining R&D · Feb 2023 – Aug 2023
Online Analyzer: CNN-Based Mineral Concentration
Prediction for Froth Flotation
📍 Marrakesh, Morocco Master's Thesis · Computer Vision · TinyML · Industry 4.0
Deployed on Edge Hardware
Final-year Master's thesis integrating Industry 4.0 into Moroccan mining. Designed, trained, and deployed a CNN-based "Online Analyzer" predicting real-time mineral concentrations (Zn, Cu, Pb, Fe) from flotation froth images replacing manual sampling with an edge-deployed vision system on a Jetson device + GigE camera. Applied CRISP-DM across three flotation circuits at the CMG Guemassa plant.
pipeline 5 stages · research + deployment
01
Domain Study & Data Collection
CRISP-DMField Work
"Understand the flotation process and capture real data"
Studied polymetallic ore separation at CMG Guemassa. Collected 80 raw videos and thousands of froth images across 3 circuits and 280+ cells over multiple shifts including documented abnormal conditions (power interruption, June 2023).
Data collected
Zn circuit: 110 samples / 11 cells
Cu circuit: 100 samples / 10 cells
Pb circuit: 70 samples / 7 cells
80 raw videos → augmented to 9,600+
Labels
✓ Cleaner: 35–56% Zn (good quality)
⚠ Rougher: 4–30% Zn (medium)
✗ Scavenger: 1–6% Zn (low quality)
✓ Courier 6i SL XRF analyzer verified
02
State-of-the-Art Review
Literature SurveyBenchmarking
"What AI approaches exist for froth flotation monitoring?"
Reviewed CV and AI methods for flotation froth monitoring. Benchmarked commercial systems (Outotec FrothSense, BGRIMM BFVS, Flovis). Identified CNN, ViT, ConvLSTM, and YOLO-based approaches from recent literature. Co-authored a paper on ViT-based soft sensor for froth quality monitoring.
03
Data Augmentation Pipeline
ConvLSTMSpatial + Temporal
"How to expand a small dataset to train deep models?"
Two-axis augmentation on the 80-video dataset. Temporal: segmented 60s videos into 12-frame sequences (2-frame shift) → 4,800 segments. Spatial: cropped 1200×1200 frames into four 400×400 quadrants → ×4 expansion. Combined: 80 videos → 9,600+ training sequences.
Augmentation result
Original: 80 videos
After temporal: 4,800 segments
After spatial: 19,200 sequences
After brightness ±0.5%: 9,600 clips
Validation (σZn)
✓ Spatial σ = 0.373 (consistent)
✓ Temporal σ = 0.503 (stable)
✓ No bias introduced by augmentation
04
CNN Regression Concentration Prediction
Deep LearningImage Cropping
"Can a CNN predict zinc grade directly from froth images?"
Trained a CNN regression model to predict zinc concentration from froth images. Compared two preprocessing pipelines with and without image cropping. Cropping proved critical: focused the model on froth texture rather than background noise. Results showed dramatic improvement across all metrics with cropping enabled.
Without cropping
R² = 0.50 · MAE = 9.32
MSE = 142.99 · RMSE = 11.96
MAPE = 0.79
With cropping ✓
R² = 0.82 · MAE = 5.38
MSE = 51.48 · RMSE = 7.18
MAPE = 0.29 (3× better)
05
CNN Classifier Froth Cell Type (Deployed)
5-Conv CNNK-Fold · K=5TinyML Jetson
"Classify froth as Cleaner / Scavenger / Rougher in real time"
Designed a 5-layer CNN (20.6M parameters) for 3-class froth classification. Trained on 4,320 images with K-Fold (K=5), Adam, lr=0.001, 50 epochs + early stopping. Deployed on a Jetson edge device with GigE camera for real-time inference at the flotation plant.
